blocks.content: The chemical classification proposed by Edward Suess divides the Earth's interior into three concentric layers: SIAL, SIMA, and NIFE based on prevailing elements.

items: SIAL is lighter and less dense than SIMA, which explains why continental crust floats over oceanic crust.
The presence of Nickel and Iron (NIFE) in the core is primarily responsible for Earth's magnetic field and high central density.
Density increases systematically from SIAL (2.7 g/cm³) down to SIMA (2.9–4.7 g/cm³) and reaches maximum in NIFE (11–13 g/cm³).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Edward Suess categorized the Earth's interior into three distinct chemical layers: SIAL, SIMA, and NIFE.
SIAL forms the upper continental crust, rich in Silica and Aluminium, with an average density of 2.7 g/cm³.
SIMA constitutes the oceanic crust and lower crust, dominated by Silica and Magnesium, with a density ranging between 2.9 and 4.7 g/cm³.
NIFE forms the innermost core composed of heavy metals Nickel (Ni) and Ferrum/Iron (Fe), responsible for Earth's magnetic field.
